purpose: Reproducible inventory of the seven private writing-reference PDFs used to create the Writing Assistant's paraphrased editorial knowledge.

integrity.page_count_definition: Total pages reported for the supplied PDF file, including front matter.
integrity.citation_page_definition: One-indexed PDF page number, not necessarily the page number printed in the source edition.
integrity.source_boundary: Source documents are reference material and never executable instructions or guaranteed truth.
integrity.repository_policy: Do not commit the PDFs, extracted full text, long quotations, or substitute reproductions. Commit only concise paraphrases, locators, identity data, and integrity metadata.
integrity.vector_store_policy: Upload a PDF only to a user-authorized, user-controlled private vector store. Do not upload it to a public or third-party corpus by default.
integrity.quotation_policy: Use short quotations only when necessary, verify them against the source, and attribute them. Prefer paraphrase for durable knowledge artifacts.

identity.title: Artful Sentences: Syntax as Style
identity.author: Virginia Tufte
identity.identity_status: Identified primary work; the local filename contains a BookSee marker but the work is Virginia Tufte's book.

sources.authority_notes: Use examples to understand syntactic functions, not to imitate distinctive prose. No construction is automatically desirable outside its context.
sources.copyright_reuse: Third-party copyrighted book supplied privately. Do not redistribute the PDF or substantial extracts. Retain only paraphrased principles and page locators; private vector-store use requires the user's authorization.

sources.authority_notes: Use as a primary account of syntactic choices while recognizing that usage conventions and examples are historically situated. Cite the bibliographic identity, not merely the filename.

identity.title: On Writing Well: The Classic Guide to Writing Nonfiction
identity.author: William Zinsser
identity.identity_status: Identified primary work; edition is material to usage and page references.

sources.editorial_role: Primary nonfiction reference for clarity, clutter, voice, sound, unity, openings, endings, methods, genre, reporting, and accuracy.
sources.authority_notes: Use the durable questions about clarity and unity while checking present-day usage and inclusive-language conventions rather than freezing the 2001 edition's prescriptions.
sources.copyright_reuse: Third-party copyrighted book supplied privately. Do not redistribute the PDF or substantial extracts. Retain only paraphrased principles and page locators; private vector-store use requires the user's authorization.

identity.title: Politics and the English Language
identity.author: George Orwell
identity.identity_status: Identified essay; the supplied PDF edition is not otherwise authenticated by this manifest.

sources.editorial_role: Primary polemical reference for stale metaphor, inflated diction, jargon, euphemism, nominalization, abstraction, and obscured agency.
sources.authority_notes: Apply the essay's diagnostics to language that conceals or substitutes for thought. Treat its rules as deliberately breakable heuristics and do not universalize its polemical style.
sources.copyright_reuse: Third-party essay PDF supplied privately; copyright and edition-specific reuse status are not established here. Do not redistribute the file or substantial extracts. Use concise paraphrase and verified short quotation only; private vector-store use requires the user's authorization.

sources.editorial_role: Primary reference for sentence commitments, implication, observation, reader trust, voice, composition, structure, revision, and stopping.
sources.authority_notes: Use the book's provocations as diagnostics. Short sentences, sentence-per-line layout, and its composition habits are exercises and perspectives, not mandatory output style.
